title: Associate Director, Biomarker Program Management
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
The Precision Medicine (PMed) Immunology and Neuroscience organization at AbbVie uses advanced methods to discover biomarkers and implement translational strategies to advance AbbVie’s innovative Immunology and Neuroscience pipeline.
The Associate Director, Biomarker Program Management, leads a team within the Immunology and Neuroscience therapeutic area that connects science and operations to manage biomarker research for multiple Phase 1-3 clinical trials. This role provides vision for operational and logistical strategies to ensure clinical trials are executed with quality and efficiency, on-time, within budget, and meet objectives. The Associate Director achieves these objectives via scientific expertise, strategic thinking, a global mindset, team building and cross-functional collaboration. This role can be based in North Chicago, IL, Waltham, MA, or South San Francisco, CA.
Responsibilities:
Lead team of Biomarker Project Managers and Sample Operations Managers to facilitate the implementation of PMed research into AbbVie clinical trials. Provide management and mentoring for team members; responsible for developing the expertise of team members. Set a positive and motivating work environment that encourages mutual respect, innovation, and accountability at all levels.
Assign approved programs and trials to team members and ensure team members are resourced, trained, and employed to start up, manage and close clinical trials. This includes partnering with PMed Biomarker Leads and being responsible for editing clinical documents, sample management, data management, cross-functional teams, budget management and strategy documents. Programs are executed to meet required timelines, budgets, and regulatory requirements. May directly manage key clinical projects within PMed.
Manage biomarker operations and logistics to support the clinical trial schedule. Proactively identify, resolve, mitigate, and/or escalate biomarker study-related risks and issues.
Ensure vendors are managed per AbbVie procedures including selection, contract execution and management. Assist in the management of Oncology budgets, ensuring accurate projections are provided to Finance monthly, quarterly, and yearly, adjusting as appropriate to keep actual variances low.
Help set Vision for Biomarker Program Management group that enables continuous improvement in processes and efficiency. Explore potential opportunities for expanding services and capabilities of BPM. Identify gaps and spearhead special development projects, as needed.
Serve as liaison with leaders of cross-functional stakeholders within AbbVie. Responsible for collaborating with personnel in other Precision Medicine groups to drive consistency within and between groups.
Apply and adhere to ICH/GCP, biosample storage procedures, biosample management best practices and ethical guidelines.
Ph.D. Degree with 8+ years project management, life science and/or clinical trial experience or Master’s Degree with 10+ years project management, life science and/or clinical trial experience or Bachelor’s Degree with 14+ years of project management, life science and/or clinical trial experience
Excellent oral and written communication skills in English. Expertise in MS Office applications including Excel, Word, Project and PowerPoint.
Organization, attention to detail and effective time management with an ability to adapt to changing priorities. Excellent analytical and interpersonal skills. Experience interacting with various levels within the organization as well as vendors.
Proven success in running meetings, working collaboratively in a cross-functional environment, and driving for success
3+ years of people management experience. Effective people management and leadership skills with a proven ability to foster team productivity and cohesiveness.
Preferred:
PMP certification desired.
Competent in application of standard business procedures (standard operating procedures, International Conference on Harmonization {ICH}, Global Regulations, Ethics and Compliance)
Experience working in a quality control and regulatory-rich environment. Experience holding meetings by teleconference and working with colleagues remotely.
Scientific background and knowledge of biomarkers. Exposure to companion diagnostic development. Knowledge of image data and associated testing.
Key Leadership Competencies:
Builds strong relationships with peers and cross-functionally with partners outside of team to enable higher performance
Learns fast, grasps the “essence,” and can change course quickly when required
Raises the bar and is never satisfied with the status quo
Creates a learning environment, open to suggestions and experimentation for improvement
Embraces the ideas of others, nurtures innovation and manages innovation to reality
Thinks beyond the program being managed to the strategy and operations of the broader Precision Medicine organization and the Development division
Act as a thought leader and mentor for team members; seek to develop the skillsets of others

The compensation range described below is the range of possible base pay compensation that the Company believes in good faith it will pay for this role at the time of this posting based on the job grade for this position. Individual compensation paid within this range will depend on many factors including geographic location, and we may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range. This range may be modified in the future. ​

The Associate Director, Immunology Payer Strategy will lead U.S. payer marketing strategy development and execution for the anticipated launches of RINVOQ and lutikizumab in hidradenitis suppurativa (HS). The role will translate payer insights, clinical and economic evidence, and access trends into asset-specific value propositions, customer narratives, and engagement plans that support launch readiness and sustained brand performance.
In partnership with the Director, Payer Strategy, the Associate Director will integrate payer needs into brand planning, evidence priorities, customer engagement, and commercial execution. This individual will lead the HS market access marketing plan across both assets, coordinate cross-functional launch preparation, and adapt strategy as evidence, customer needs, and the access environment evolve. The role requires strategic thinking, financial acumen, and strong cross-functional influence.
Key Responsibilities
Collaborate with cross function partners to develop and deliver disease-state education, resource training, and launch preparation that enable consistent, appropriate customer conversations.
Lead the marketing workstream for appropriate preapproval information exchange resources in partnership with medical, regulatory, legal, and compliance.
Develop differentiated, evidence-based payer messaging  by leveraging clinical data, health economic outcomes research, real-world evidence, treatment guidelines, and market performance data. Ensure that payer messages are relevant to customer needs and aligned with the overall payer strategy
Identify and prioritize evidence and RWE needs  by assessing evidence gaps, defining payer-relevant evidence priorities, and partnering with Medical, HEOR, and other stakeholders to support development and translation of an integrated evidence strategy
Drive resource development through effective agency management; ensure appropriate governance and compliance  by partnering with Legal, Regulatory, and Compliance to ensure that payer claims and materials are appropriately supported and consistent with applicable requirements
Track launch-readiness milestones and, following approval, account activation and formulary adoption with analytics partners; synthesize field insights and provide recommendations for commercial leadership and business reviews.
Influence without direct authority  by building productive relationships, driving timely decisions, mediating cross-functional issues, and communicating recommendations effectively to stakeholders and senior leaders
Demonstrate a  “One AbbVie” mindset  by considering enterprise priorities, seeking opportunities to leverage learning across brands and therapeutic areas, and sharing effective approaches across the broader Market Access organization
Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree required.
5–7 years of experience in Market Access, Marketing, and/or Immunology
Ability to interpret clinical and scientific information and apply it to payer marketing strategy, value proposition development, and tactical execution.
Knowledge of the U.S. payer environment, commercial and government channels, formulary decision-making, utilization management, and specialty medicine reimbursement dynamics
Demonstrated cross-functional leadership and influence in a matrixed organization, with strong project management, prioritization, and adaptability.
Experience managing agencies or vendors, project timelines, budgets, and material review processes.
Preferred Qualifications
Master’s degree or other relevant advanced degree.
3 years of U.S. Market Access experience.
Experience in immunology, dermatology, or HS, and familiarity with specialty medicines and biosimilar competition.
Experience supporting a U.S. product launch or indication expansion, including prelaunch planning, field readiness, and postlaunch optimization.
Experience coordinating marketing strategy across multiple assets or indications.
Cross-functional experience in account management, brand marketing, patient services, trade and channel strategy, HEOR, or market research and analytics.

title: Advanced Analytics Intern
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join:
Airbnb is seeking an Advanced Analytics Intern to join the Finance Data Science & Strategy team within the Finance organization for the 2027 Summer Intern Program.
The Finance Data Science & Strategy team builds the statistical models behind Airbnb’s top line forecast and explains how the business performs against it. The work runs as a loop. We figure out where actuals differ from forecast and why, share the answer with partners across Finance and the business, and feed what we learned into the next version of the forecast, so each cycle starts from a better baseline than the last.
We are looking for someone curious about business and data, who can understand both the ‘what’ and the ‘why’ behind a number and help translate them into decisions. An ideal candidate would have some familiarity with analytical methodologies, BI tooling, and business communication.
The Difference You Will Make:
As an Advanced Analytics Intern on our team, you’ll help explain how the business performed against the forecast and use what you find to improve it. You’ll have the opportunity to:
Build comprehensive and high quality analyses of how the business is performing against the forecast, and explain what drove the difference
Work with the team’s data scientists to turn those findings into improvements in the next version of the forecast
Communicate findings clearly to partners across Finance and the business, in written readouts and recurring reviews
A Typical Day:
During your internship you’ll be integrated into a team where you’ll contribute to challenging projects. Your manager, team, and our incredible employee community will strive to be superhosts to you during the summer. We provide the support, mentorship, fun, and real world experience needed to accelerate your learning and make a real impact on our business, as Airbnb revolutionizes connection, belonging, and travel. You’ll be expected to:
Own and complete a capstone project from beginning to end
Collaborate with multiple team members to achieve project milestones
Communicate with stakeholders across different teams to provide project updates
Seek and provide feedback throughout the internship
Actively participate in and contribute to the Finance Data Science & Strategy team and broader Airbnb community
Your Expertise:
This opportunity is for full-time students completing a Master’s degree in a quantitative field (e.g. Data Science, Mathematics, Analytics, Statistics, Econometrics, etc.) with at least one semester of school remaining after the internship.
Proficient in communication and collaboration, with the ability to effectively engage with diverse teams and individuals
Skilled in conducting thorough and inclusive analyses, ensuring that findings are communicated clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Possesses robust data, statistical analysis, and analytics skills, contributing to a comprehensive understanding of complex datasets.
Substantial experience in SQL, along with a solid foundation in at least one programming language (Python or R)
Preferred (not required): Familiarity with forecasting, time series, and/or A/B testing

title: Senior Technical Program Manager, Robot Evaluation Operations, Robot Evaluation Operations
description:
Fauna Robotics is building capable, safe, and delightful robots for everyday life. Before a new skill reaches a customer’s home, we need to know how well it works: how often it succeeds, how fast it is, and where it fails, across the range of homes and conditions our customers live in. We are hiring a Senior Technical Program Manager to run the operation that produces that evidence.
In this role, you will own robot evaluation operations end to end, in lab and home environments. Our scientists define what to measure; you make it happen at scale, on schedule, and with results the team can trust. You will turn evaluation requests from science and engineering into planned campaigns, keep robots, test environments, and operators ready, and deliver results that leaders use to decide what ships. You will treat evaluation as a production operation with measurable output, not a support function.
Key job responsibilities
- Own the evaluation program from intake to results: take requests from science and engineering teams, prioritize them against shared robot and lab capacity, and publish the campaign schedule
- Run evaluation campaigns in lab and home environments, with clear entry and exit criteria and standard run procedures
- Build and maintain the physical test environments: home-like lab setups, object and fixture inventories, scene resets, and versioned configurations so results stay comparable across software releases and robot hardware revisions
- Stand up in-home evaluation operations with legal, privacy, safety, and research partners, including scheduling, data handling, and on-site safety procedures
- Direct the work of evaluation operators and vendor teams: training and certification, shift coverage, and scoring standards that stay consistent across raters and sites
- Partner with hardware and fleet teams on robot availability for testing, including maintenance windows, repairs, and per-unit acceptance runs
- Enforce logging and traceability standards so every evaluation trial is reproducible and accounted for
- Deliver results as a product: standard scorecards and dashboards, triage of failures to the right owning team, and evidence that feeds launch and release go/no-go decisions
- Track throughput, valid-trial yield, cost per trial, and turnaround time, own the evaluation budget, and identify manual evaluations that are ready for automation or simulation
- Present evaluation status, risks, and tradeoffs to senior leadership, and say “not yet” when demand exceeds capacity
About the team
Fauna Robotics, an Amazon company, is building capable, safe, and genuinely delightful robots for everyday life. Our goal is simple: make robots people actually want to live and interact with in everyday human spaces.
We believe that future won’t arrive until building for robotics becomes far more accessible. Today, too much effort is spent reinventing the fundamentals. We’re changing that by developing tightly integrated hardware and software systems that make it faster, safer, and more intuitive to create real-world robotic products.
Our work spans the full stack: mechanical design, control systems, dynamic modeling, and intelligent software. The focus is not just functionality, but experience. We’re building robots that feel responsive, expressive, and genuinely useful.
At Fauna, you’ll work at the frontier of this space, helping define how robots move, manipulate, and interact with people in natural environments. It’s an opportunity to solve hard problems across hardware and software with a team focused on making robotics accessible and joyful to build.
If you care about making robotics real for everyone and building systems that are as delightful as they are capable, we’re interested in hearing from you.

- 7+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, a related field, or equivalent experience
- Experience running test, validation, evaluation, or field operations programs for physical products such as robots, autonomous vehicles, or consumer devices
- Experience managing vendors, contractors, or operations teams that execute work on a schedule
Preferred qualifications: - Experience evaluating machine learning models or robot policies, or running data collection operations for robot learning
- Experience providing evidence for Go/No-Go or launch-readiness decisions
- Experience running tests in homes or with members of the public, including privacy and safety procedures
- Familiarity with experiment design and statistics, such as trial counts, confidence intervals, and scoring consistency across raters
- Ability to analyze data with SQL or Python and build dashboards
- Experience with simulation-based testing or hardware-in-the-loop test programs

description:

No two months in this role look the same. The data keeps growing, the tools keep changing, and there's always a new challenge worth taking on. It's a great fit for someone who likes to work independently, dig into complex problems, and see their work make a difference across a team.

description:

title: Autonomy Simulation Engineer
description:
About the Team
DoorDash Labs is an independent team within DoorDash. We explore robotics and automation to transform last-mile logistics in the long term. If you have a passion for applying robotics solutions in a service used by millions of people, then we want to talk to you!
About the Role
The Simulation team builds software, models, and environments to test on-road autonomous robot behavior and evaluate autonomy changes before deployment. We are hiring an Autonomy Simulation Engineer to improve simulation fidelity and accelerate the development and validation of autonomous delivery robots.
You will develop production simulation software and models of robot behavior and interactions with the environment, using real-world data and repeatable experiments to calibrate and validate them. Working closely with autonomy and robotics engineers, you will own projects from design through validation and report to the Simulation Lead. We expect this role to be hybrid, with some time in-office and some time remote.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Develop and maintain the simulation engine and supporting software.
Build and improve simulation models of robot behavior, other participants, and their interactions.
Calibrate and validate simulation models against real-world behavior using controlled, repeatable experiments.
Develop parameterized environments and synthetic scenarios to test conditions and interactions that are difficult to capture in the field.
Investigate differences between simulated and real-world behavior, identify contributing model assumptions and parameters, and implement improvements.
Improve simulator reproducibility, reliability, usability, and debuggability.
We’re excited about you because…
You have strong production C++ and Python experience.
You can translate real-world behavior and physical systems into practical software models.
You have experience building closed-loop or interactive simulation software, with depth in areas such as robot dynamics, physics, road-user behavior, synthetic scenario generation, or probabilistic modeling.
You have used real-world data and controlled, repeatable experiments to test, calibrate, or validate software models.
You have experience debugging complex systems and delivering reliable production software using Linux, Git, automated testing, and CI.
Experience applying machine learning to simulation modeling and validating learned models against real-world data is a plus.

As a Shift Lead, you will have shift responsibility for fulfilling orders in a warehouse environment and maintaining inventory, and in some locations, this involves preparing food in a light-prep kitchen.

description:
About MISUMI Americas
MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.
Impact In This Role
The Executive Assistant is the operational engine behind the President & CEO’s day. This person owns the calendar, travel and inbox so the President & CEO can focus on the highest priorities, and handles scheduling requests from across the company. The role also prepares itineraries for multi-day trips and events involving the President & CEO, and supports company events.
The role sits in the Office of the CEO team and reports to the Chief of Staff, while serving as executive assistant to the President & CEO. Because the role sees very sensitive information, discretion is essential.
What You’ll Be Doing
Executive & Calendar Support
Own President & CEO's calendar end-to-end — complex scheduling, prioritization, and proactive management of conflicts across multiple time zones
Anticipate scheduling needs before they arise; protect time for high-priority work and thinking
Prepare President & CEO for meetings with relevant context, briefings, and materials
Manage high-volume email; draft correspondence, flag action items, and ensure timely follow-through
Coordinate and manage complex meeting cadences across the Executive Leadership Team and extended leadership organization, including agenda preparation, pre-read distribution, and post-meeting action item tracking to ensure decisions are captured and followed through
Coordinate closely with the Chief of Staff to align on priorities and ensure nothing is missed
Travel Planning & Logistics
Plan and book complex domestic and international travel — flights, hotels, ground transport, visas — often on short notice with changing itineraries
Travel with President & CEO on select high-priority trips to provide on-the-ground support
Build detailed travel itineraries and anticipate logistics at every step
Manage travel expenses and reconcile reports accurately and on time
Meeting & Event Coordination
Coordinate executive leadership team meetings and offsites, including gathering agendas, logistics, and tracking follow-ups
Support All Hands meetings and company-wide events — managing AV, Zoom, run of show, and speaker coordination
Manage conference room calendars and troubleshoot tech issues in real time
Administrative & Special Projects
Maintain and update critical documentation, expense reports, and organizational records
Support confidential projects with the highest level of discretion
Assist with external relations, executive outreach, and stakeholder communications as needed
Take on special projects at the direction of President & CEO and the Chief of Staff
Please note: All employees are expected to maintain and contribute to the QMS.
Desired Traits
5+ years of executive assistant experience, ideally supporting a C-suite executive in a fast-paced tech or startup environment
Discreet and trustworthy: handles sensitive personal and professional information with complete professionalism
Exceptionally organized, with a bias toward systems and proactive planning
Clear communicator, written and verbal, who can represent the President & CEO's voice when needed
Calm under pressure and decisive when priorities change
Comfortable managing up: keeps a busy executive on track without overstepping
Tech-driven: proficient with Microsoft Teams, Google Workspace, Slack, Zoom and travel booking platforms, picks up new tools quickly, and uses AI to support and improve workflows
Resourceful and self-directed: finds solutions before problems become visible
Able to work on site with the Office of the CEO team
Japanese language proficiency is a plus, but not required
Physical Demands
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Primarily office-based work with prolonged computer use.
Occasionally lifts event materials of up to 25 lbs.
Up to 25% domestic and international travel to support the President & CEO on select trips and to support company events.
Perks and Benefits
Competitive medical, dental, and vision insurance
401K plan
Parental leave programs
Paid volunteer days
And much, much more!

Bring diverse perspectives and experience to our culture and company.

Thrive in an environment emphasizing respect, honesty, collaboration, and growth.

Help us continue to build a world-class organization that values the contributions of all of our teammates

title: Associate Category Manager
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
Manages supply chain of assigned direct materials suppliers and parts to support business continuity and optimization, including sourcing, supporting development of category strategy roadmaps, supporting contract negotiation, analyzing spend, creating inventory management strategies, gathering commodity intelligence, and managing supplier performance; may include limited management of purchase orders.
May lead cross-functional category team
Identifies and may support implementation of key continuous improvement initiatives
Essential Job Duties
Category Management
Supports creation of long-term supplier strategies and roadmaps in collaboration with manager. Engages with internal stakeholders to learn about their needs and influence category strategy with manager to align with long-term business objectives.
Co-leads direct procurement supplier selection process with collaboration from Supplier Engineering and oversight from manager. Uses strategic sourcing practices to identify a core supply base able to offer lowest total cost of ownership and high-quality product while identifying value improvement opportunities.
Supports manager with alignment of production supplier requirements and sourcing strategies with those of new product development (NPI) for designated suppliers/categories to ensure uninterrupted material availability, alignment of risk, and cost goals with long term vision for the category / business
Ensures assigned category team goals and objectives are achieved
Engages with manager and cross-functional peers to understand and share market trends and commodity intelligence
Supports creation of content for category strategy reviews and may present some content at these meetings
Supplier Performance Management
Leads supplier scorecarding and supplier business reviews for assigned suppliers
Collaborates with supply base and procurement team to manage demand changes to minimize excess inventory or material shortages
Leads continuous improvement efforts needed with suppliers
Risk and Capacity Management
Proposes mitigation plans for assigned suppliers and critical sub-tier suppliers and supports implementation in collaboration with manager and cross-functional peers
Leads capacity assessments for assigned suppliers and critical sub-tier suppliers
May serve as project manager for key supplier capacity or risk mitigation initiatives
Contract and Cost Management
Under supervision of manager, utilizes established template agreements to install contracts with suppliers or amendments to existing agreements
Collaborates with manager to establish long-term volume pricing, risk mitigation, and capacity agreements with key suppliers to support Intuitive’s volume growth
Reviews, administers, and manages long-term purchase order and delivery commitments to designated suppliers as necessary to support production and/or sales requirements within the business
Leads identification of cost reduction ideas to achieve year-over-year cost goals within assigned category(ies) and may support implementation of projects
Operational Management
Supports plant purchasing by leading negotiations with suppliers to adopt and implement lean sourcing principles to enable 100% material availability and optimization of on-hand inventory levels.
Embraces continuous improvement techniques to drive toward attainment of key purchasing metrics (supplier on-time delivery, quality, risk management, inventory velocity, and cost reduction).
May lead change management/change order implementation for complex projects
Supports master data integrity for suppliers and parts
May help train new colleagues within the supply chain organization. Identifies process and training improvement opportunities and may support closure of identified gaps.
Required Skills and Experience
Strong knowledge of buying, material planning, master scheduling, and forecasting
Demonstrated negotiations experience
Significant computer experience including MS Office products and ERP systems. Strong Excel skills.
Ability to handle multiple tasks and projects successfully and adapt to changing priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing company
Thorough knowledge of and experience working with kanban systems and other lean principles
Demonstrates concern for precision and thoroughness
Proven ability to consistently achieve stretch goals and objectives
Strong verbal and written communication skills
Required Education and Training
BS degree or equivalent and 8+ years of procurement or sourcing experience in a regulated industry manufacturing environment. Master’s degree preferred.
Working Conditions
~25% travel to both domestic and international suppliers
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience in the medical device industry preferred

Familiarity with electronic test and measurement equipment such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, function generators, spectrum analyzers, and willingness to develop hands-on troubleshooting skills.
Familiarity with electronic design tools (e.g., OrCAD, Allegro, SPICE) or willingness to learn.
Basic understanding of PCB manufacturing and assembly processes.
Awareness of component selection criteria and design for safety, reliability, and manufacturability.
Ability to document findings clearly and communicate effectively with team members.

Interest in, or experience with, medical devices or other regulated industries.
Exposure to design control concepts, including design input, design output, traceability, FMEA risk analysis, and Corrective and preventive action (CAPA) investigations.
Signal integrity in mixed-signal/power environments.
Motion control or feedback control systems.
FPGA logic design, tools, and verification processes.
Familiarity with relevant business tools: Agile PLM, SAP, Polarion, JIRA, Confluence, etc.
Knowledge of C, Python, MATLAB, or other programming/scripting languages.
UL, CE, IEC 60601, and/or FDA regulatory requirements for medical devices.

Proven ability to identify issues, bring clarity and transparency, and lead a team effectively to appropriate product solutions
Comfortable with all phases of the product development lifecycle including design, implementation, debug, verification, qualification, and transfer to Manufacturing.

Demonstrated mechanical design and analysis skills, including statics, dynamics, kinematics, strength of materials and stress analysis
Strong understanding of component selection criteria and materials as they relate to design and manufacturability
Experience with design for reliability, manufacturability, and assembly
Comfortable operating machine shop, measurement and test equipment
Ability to communicate effectively (written, oral) across all levels and organizations
Ability to mentor other engineers
Ability to travel up to 10% time
A real excitement to learn and get to the bottom of tough technical problems

BSME required with 5+ years or MSME (preferred) with 3+ years of industry experience in developing commercial mechanical and electromechanical robotic products

Surgical or medical device product experience is a plus.
Effective collaboration with multi-disciplinary functions like clinical, human factors, industrial design, interaction design, etc.
Comfortable using Matlab, Python, or similar software
Demonstrated knowledge and experience with metal casting manufacturing processes and parts are a strong plus.

Regulatory agency experience including UL, CE, and FDA approval processes

It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of the Position
The Senior Clinical Development Engineer (CDE) uses their in-depth knowledge of the surgical environment and medical technology to work with design engineers and clinicians to define, develop, and validate the clinical function of new products within our single-port robotic platforms. The primary focus of the CDE is to establish and validate data-driven clinical requirements to ensure a high-quality patient outcome.
Essential Job Duties
​​ Apply in-depth knowledge of the operating room environment and of the da Vinci Surgical Systems to become an expert within the company on the clinical application of Intuitive’s products
​Provide a clinical voice to product development by defining and assessing clinical performance of new products
​Collaborate with marketing partners and clinicians to identify and understand clinical needs
​Use an analytical approach to identify potential product enhancements and new product ideas
​Take an active role in new product development teams, including contributing to design reviews, and providing design guidance to engineering design teams
​Assess and document clinical risks, and identify appropriate mitigations
​Conduct pre-clinical testing to validate the safety and efficacy of new products
​Support regulatory documentation and submissions
​Provide subject matter expertise to user manual and training documentation development
​Support clinical evaluation of new products at key customer sites
​Maintain current knowledge of clinical applications of Intuitive’s products
​Keep Intuitive’s vision and values at the forefront of decision making
​Perform other duties as required to support the company’s overall strategy and goals
Required Skills and Experience
​ Minimum of 8 years of experience in medical device industry with a Bachelor’s degree, 6 years experience with a Master’s degree, or 3 years with a PhD degree
Proven experience in supporting a medical product from design to launch
​Experience working with surgeons in an operating room environment
​Fluent in surgical terminology and sound knowledge of anatomy and surgical technique
VoC experience with sugeons to discuss products and workflow
​Excellent mechanical aptitude and intuition for spatial relations, including the ability to understand complex mechanical products
Nice to haves:
​Excellent analytical capability and practical skills to develop test methods and draw conclusions
​Excellent teamwork skills with proven ability to cultivate collaboration across multiple disciplines
​Effective communication skills (verbal, written, presentation)
​Proven success recognizing critical issues and driving them to closure by taking coordinated action
​Self-starter needing minimal supervision
​Self-confident and able to react quickly under pressure
Required Education and Training
​​ Minimum of Bachelor of Science degree in Mechanical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, or similar; advanced degree preferred
Working Conditions ​
Ability to travel up to 25% of the time, internationally and domestic

description:

If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
The Senior Electrical Engineer will maintain, improve, and support existing surgical devices for the da Vinci Multiport Surgical System throughout their product lifecycle. The successful candidate will manage component obsolescence, drive design improvements for reliability and cost, investigate and resolve field and manufacturing issues, and ensure ongoing regulatory compliance - all while upholding the highest product quality standards.
Responsibilities
Manage component obsolescence - Identify, source, and evaluate alternates, and drive qualification and implementation of replacements.
Execute design changes - Author, review, and implement Engineering Change Orders (ECOs), updating schematics, PCB layouts, wiring diagrams, BOMs, design history files (DHFs), specifications, test procedures, and FMEAs.
Support manufacturing and production – Support Manufacturing and Test Engineering in troubleshooting PCBA assembly issues, identifying and resolving any design-related problems.
Drive cost reduction and reliability improvements - Identify and implement design optimizations that reduce product cost or improve field reliability.
Investigate and resolve field issues - Lead root cause analysis on product complaints, field failures, and manufacturing defects related to electrical/electronic subsystems.
Ensure ongoing regulatory compliance - Verify that all design changes meet applicable safety, EMC, and regulatory standards within design control requirements.
Partner with suppliers and cross-functional teams - Work with Supplier Engineering, Quality, Procurement, Manufacturing, Field Service, and Regulatory teams to qualify alternate suppliers, resolve incoming quality and product issues efficiently.
Serve as subject matter expert - Own the design intent of legacy products and provide technical guidance and mentorship to junior engineers.
Required Education, Skills & Experience
Minimum 8 years of experience and a Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field; or 6 years of experience and a Master's degree; or 3 years of experience and a PhD; or equivalent work experience.
Demonstrated experience with sustaining engineering activities, including root cause analysis and engineering change management.
Hands-on ability to characterize and troubleshoot complex electronic systems in the field or on the production line, using oscilloscopes, multimeters, function generators, spectrum analyzers, and custom test platforms.
Proficiency with electronic design tools (e.g., OrCAD, Allegro, SPICE).
Demonstrated knowledge of PCB manufacturing and assembly processes.
Understanding of component selection criteria and design for safety, reliability, and manufacturability.
Experience with design control concepts, including design input, design output, traceability, and FMEA risk analysis.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including presenting root cause analyses and corrective action plans to audiences across all levels and functions.
Preferred Skills & Experience
Experience in medical devices or other regulated industries.
Experience with UL, CE, IEC 60601, and/or FDA regulatory requirements for medical devices.
Experience with corrective and preventive action (CAPA) investigations, driving corrective actions to closure.
Experience with signal integrity in mixed-signal/power environments.
Familiarity with motion control or feedback control systems.
Exposure to FPGA logic design, tools, and verification processes.
Proficiency with relevant business tools: Agile PLM, SAP, Polarion, JIRA, Confluence, etc.
Knowledge of C, Python, MATLAB, or other programming/scripting languages.

The Systems Mechanical Engineering team is responsible for the development of multiport da Vinci Surgical Systems from product concept through market launch and initial product stabilization.
The Senior Mechanical Engineer, Electronics Enclosure Design will focus on designing a novel compute box for use within various da Vinci system platforms. This person will need to leverage their working understanding of thermal management, electromechanical design, and design requirement definition and refinement. They will interface with multiple functions including, but not limited to, electrical engineering, systems engineering, manufacturing, procurement, supplier engineering, quality, and regulatory.
The Senior Mechanical Engineer, Electronics Enclosure Design is expected to use first-principles design methodology and analytical skills to conceptualize, develop, and verify a new compute box architecture. This person will be expected to work with various cross-functional representatives on the project, in addition to acting as the functional representative of the product. They will be expected to excel in a focused, high-energy, collaborative work environment with a team of talented engineers. The Senior Mechanical Engineer, Electronics Enclosure Design should be capable of making sound decisions when faced with time constraints and ambiguous or incomplete information typical of research and development.
Roles & Responsibilities
Own the mechanical design development of a novel electronics enclosure design
Author and release design documentation including drawings, schematics, etc.
Working with various interdisciplinary teams (electrical engineering, sustaining engineering, test engineering, field service etc.) to communicate effectively and bring consensus on complex problems
Working within multi-disciplinary teams to negotiate requirements
Designing for EMC compliance, manufacturability, reliability, serviceability, and cost
Selecting and managing vendors in the prototype phase
Collaborating with manufacturing to create product assembly tooling, fixtures, and instructions
Developing and performing component verification testing
Supporting production of final product by troubleshooting process and component problems
Providing engineering support to Manufacturing, Materials, Test Engineering, and Service to facilitate transfer of designs
Rapid development and iteration of full-scale prototypes of candidate architectures to satisfy requirements
Drive design improvements through DFM and failure analysis
Mentor and coach other engineers in problem solving
Skills, Experience, Education, & Training
Required
Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, or similar
7+ years of experience with mechanical design or machine design in a regulated industry (medical device, aerospace, spacecraft, defense, etc.)
Deep understanding of design controls: design inputs & outputs, risks, design verification, and change control
Passion for details in creating robust and reliable machines designed for mission-critical applications
Ability to apply knowledge of thermal management and engineering materials and criteria to productize designs through strong concept development, design analysis, hands-on prototyping, and reliability testing skills
Proficiency using CAD, analysis, and finite element simulation tools to design mechanical assemblies
Excellent communication skills , interpersonal skills, and the ability to receive and implement performance feedback
Self-driven with the ability to excel in a high-energy, small, focused team environment, to maintain a strong sense of shared responsibility and shared reward, and to make work fun and interesting
Preferred
Surgical or medical device product experience
Thermal simulation experience (ANSYS Icepak)
Comfortable with all phases of the product development lifecycle including design, implementation, debug, verification, qualification, and transfer
Experience designing for volume manufacturing processes such as metal castings, injection molding, sheet metal stamping, compression molding, thermoforming, etc.
SolidWorks experience

Primary Function of Position
The Staff Mechanical Design Engineer independently owns technically demanding mechanical and electromechanical subsystems for robotic systems. You will lead subsystem architecture and detailed-design decisions, resolve complex multidisciplinary problems, and contribute to integration decisions beyond your assigned subsystem.
This is a hands-on individual contributor role combining mechanical design ownership with technical guidance and mentorship. The role reports to a Manager of Mechanical Design Engineering in New Product Development.
Essential Job Duties
Own subsystem development from concept through verification and design transfer, including mechanical requirements, specifications, design-risk analyses and verification documentation. Support validation activities with the responsible functions.

description:

Experience in optical and opto-mechanical tolerance analysis
Experience in designing molded plastic optics and light pipes, using non-sequential ray trace CAD tools

Experience in practical lab methods to test optical phenomena associated with light sources, spatial light modulators, and complex optical systems

description:
Job Description:
Job Description
We believe the world we want tomorrow starts with how we do business today, which is the vision at the heart of Mars’ Sustainable in a Generation Plan, one where the planet is healthy, people and pets are thriving, and society is inclusive.
The Assistant General Counsel, Sustainability (Human Rights & Supply Chain Due Diligence) will play a senior role on the enterprise-level Sustainability Legal team at Mars, Inc. This role serves as the global legal lead for business and human rights and supply chain due diligence within Mars.
This is a high-visibility role in a small headquarters team. The role acts as a subject-matter lead within the enterprise Sustainability Legal framework, setting legal strategy, guardrails, governance approaches, and escalation protocols for human-rights-related risks and regulations. The successful candidate will be a senior, independent lawyer who can influence without authority, build trust across a complex global organization, and provide clear, practical advice in a rapidly evolving regulatory environment.
What will be your key responsibilities?
Provide senior legal advice on global business and human rights, responsible sourcing, and supply chain due diligence issues affecting Mars across segments, regions, and functions.
Lead enterprise legal strategy for human-rights and supply-chain-due-diligence-related regulations and legal risks, including enterprise interpretation, legal guardrails, governance frameworks, and escalation protocols.
Serve as the subject-matter lead for human rights within Mars’ enterprise Sustainability Legal framework and help shape a One-Mars legal approach in this area.
Lead or support legal workstreams relating to material sustainability regulations in the role’s subject-matter area, including the CSRD, CS3D, LkSG, EUDR, FLR and other forced labor and responsible sourcing regulations and related emerging global developments.
Support high-risk issues, investigations, and escalations relating to business and human rights, responsible sourcing, and supply chain due diligence matters.
Develop, sponsor, or oversee practical legal guidance, policies, playbooks, templates, training, and governance tools in the role’s subject-matter area, working closely with other Sustainability Legal team members to support scalable implementation across segments and regions.
Partner closely with segment and regional legal teams to align on enterprise legal positions, promote consistent application of human rights legal standards and due diligence requirements, and enable local operationalization without displacing segment or regional ownership.
Act as a trusted connector among Legal, Sustainability, Procurement, Finance, and Corporate and Public Affairs at the corporate, segment, and regional levels to promote consistent, practical, and risk-balanced legal approaches across Mars.
Advise Public Affairs and other corporate stakeholders on legal considerations arising from sustainability-related policy development, advocacy positions, external engagement, and participation in industry or multistakeholder forums where human rights or supply chain due diligence issues are implicated.
Support legal trend analysis and regulatory insights for emerging business and human rights, responsible sourcing, and supply chain due diligence laws, enforcement trends, and stakeholder expectations.
Develop and deliver training and capacity-building for legal and business stakeholders on human rights and supply chain due diligence legal risk and compliance requirements.
What are we looking for?
Law degree from an accredited university in the U.S., EU, UK, or another relevant jurisdiction.
Licensed, admitted, or otherwise qualified to practice law in at least one relevant jurisdiction.
12 to 15+ years of relevant legal experience, including significant experience advising on business and human rights, responsible sourcing, supply chain due diligence, forced labor, sustainability compliance, or related regulatory matters.
Deep knowledge of business and human rights frameworks, emerging due diligence regulations, forced labor laws, responsible sourcing programs, and human rights risk management.
Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively across adjacent sustainability legal topics, for example sustainability claims, deforestation, reporting, packaging, or other emerging regulatory issues, as part of an integrated enterprise sustainability legal model.
Experience working in-house at a global organization preferred, particularly in a matrixed environment involving corporate, segment, regional, and functional stakeholders.
Experience handling sensitive, high-risk issues, investigations, or escalations involving human rights, responsible sourcing, or supply chain due diligence matters.
Familiarity with public policy development, advocacy, or external affairs processes, including experience advising Public Affairs, Government Relations or similar teams on legal and reputational considerations related to sustainability policy matters.
Strong judgment, communication, influencing, and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to provide practical, risk-balanced advice to senior legal and business leaders.
Demonstrated ability to build alignment across functions and geographies without relying solely on formal authority.
Ability to establish and maintain clear role boundaries, clarify ownership across center, segment, and regional teams, and escalate issues appropriately while preserving collaborative relationships.

Work with over 180,000 diverse and talented Associates, all guided by Mars’ Five Principles.

Job Description:
The Supply/Capability Trainer will lead site-wide capability building and training execution across our operations and maintenance teams. In this role, you will champion a culture of continuous learning, standard work, and operational excellence by translating hands-on technical processes into clear, engaging, and modern digital and classroom learning experiences.
The ideal candidate brings strong facilitation and coaching skills, practical knowledge of manufacturing operations, and experience with Education & Training (E&T) pillar methodologies to drive safety, quality, and peak equipment performance.
What are we looking for?
Minimum Qualifications
High school diploma or GED equivalent.
2+ years of experience in a manufacturing, operations, supply chain, or technical industrial environment.
Proven experience delivering training, coaching associates, or facilitating workshops/onboarding programs.
Demonstrated ability to create clear instructional materials, standard operating procedures (SOPs), job aids, or digital training content.
Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills with the ability to engage diverse shop-floor and leadership teams.
Proficiency with digital tools, including Microsoft Office (Word, PowerPoint, Excel) and standard learning technologies.

Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Education, Technical Communications, Engineering, or a related field.
3+ years of experience in a dedicated functional training, technical writing, or organizational development role within a TPM/Lean manufacturing setting.
Experience with Education & Training (E&T) pillar concepts, Training Within Industry (TWI), Train-the-Trainer (TTT) frameworks, role profiling, or skills gap analysis.
Experience producing multimedia learning content (short instructional videos, e-learning modules, digital checklists).
Familiarity with vertical startup methodologies and project commissioning support.

Leadership & Strateg y
Team Collaboration: Participate on a team of Functional Trainers and Training Support associates as part of a high-performing, customer service-driven team.
Program Deployment: Identify, develop, and deploy site-wide training programs to address critical needs in onboarding, job qualification, safety, quality, Education & Training (E&T), and equipment operation.

Continuous Improvement: Utilize Education & Training (E&T) Pillar Essential Elements, processes, and programs to continuously improve training procedures (including OJT/TTT, Turbo Charge, Role Profiling, and Skills Gap Analysis).

Standard Work Documentation: Develop, document, and maintain standard work instructions, training materials, job aids, and checklists across both paper-based and digital formats.
Multimedia Learning: Create engaging instructional videos, e-learning modules, and presentations demonstrating standard work and correct operating procedures.

An industry competitive salary and benefits package, including company bonus.

As a CO+I Critical Environment Technician, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.    Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.    With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider. Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.    In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.   Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties

Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed and promotes a safe working culture to empower less experienced team members. Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting up to 25lbs / 11kg without assistance. Occasional lifting 25-50lbs / 11-22.5kg with lift assistance. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.

Takes part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Coordinates and schedules supplier/vendor on-site activities. Reviews and completes appropriate work orders to support approval of vendor supplier field service reports or invoices.
Prepares and submits required reports (e.g., turnover, preventative maintenance [PM]) as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates, or using ad hoc methods required to support trending and analysis (e.g., Maintenance data, equipment trending data). Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for devices and disciplines within their coverage and expertise to ensure safe and reliable execution. Documents completed work using approved tools and procedural templates for more experienced technician review. Completes and provides coaching to support less experienced technicians for mandatory, technical, and procedural training assignments. Analyzes findings from reports and documents observations.
Performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs following methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for multiple disciplines and one or more types of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, cooling systems) with minimal supervision - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Performs maintenance tasks and repairs that can be performed with minimal oversight. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Oversees maintenance tasks within a single discipline or area of expertise. Maintains all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance with established mastery of maintaining systems of a specific discipline.
Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Determines when troubleshooting efforts are deemed adequate and communicates or escalates to suppliers, engineers, or more experienced colleagues as needed. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment works within disciplines they have been trained and how to troubleshoot to a subsystem level. Provides consultation to less experienced colleagues with troubleshooting systems and problems. May lead efforts to troubleshoot issues and identify root causes.
Processes method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Coordinates activities and associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities.

Tracks hours for performed tasks within applicable task management systems. Adds required data, documents, logs changes, and upkeeps procedures related to building management systems and reports. Properly signals spare equipment and parts utilization within maintenance work orders.
Works on advanced tasks (e.g., vendor contact, escalations) independently. Serves as a subject matter expert in critical environments-related systems within the data center, and advises less experienced colleagues on such topics. Possesses an understanding of and operates equipment and systems within a set discipline (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls) with knowledge of the interactions between them and overall operation of a data center. Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner.
Inspects and supervises critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning [HVAC], mechanical systems), building, and grounds for unsafe or abnormal conditions to develop and analyze trends. Understands critical system alarms for single discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (i.e., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) within the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify all alarms. Uses technical expertise, prior experience, and device analytics to recognize trends with equipment behavior and checks potential issues as they arise. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems. Performs all monitoring equipment repair, replacement, and maintenance work, which meets or exceeds Microsoft Service Level Agreement (SLA) requirements.
Safety and quickly responds to and leads an onsite incident response team for all abnormal conditions that impact operations, and coordinates with other critical facilities professionals to perform corrective repairs, without supervision. title: Director of Datacenter IT Operations
description:
Overview
Microsoft's Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. It delivers the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services, including Bing, Microsoft 365, Xbox, OneDrive and the Microsoft Azure platform. Our infrastructure is a global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. It supports more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries.
Reporting to the Charlotte Metro Director, the Director of Datacenter IT Operations is the senior IT Operations leader for the Charlotte Metro. This leader owns end-to-end IT operations, IT outfitting and IT infrastructure delivery across all Class A and Class B datacenter facilities in the metro. That organization is accountable for safe, secure, on-time and defect-free delivery of customer capacity, and for reliable, SLA-compliant operation of IT infrastructure once it is live.
The role covers the full IT lifecycle. That starts with design input and construction coordination, continues through IT outfitting, network and server deployment, operational readiness and turnover, and extends into steady-state operations, hardware lifecycle management and decommissioning. The Director partners closely with Critical Environment (CE), IAM/Logistics, Datacenter Delivery (DCD), Datacenter Engineering (DCE), Commissioning, network and hardware engineering teams, and vendors. Together they ensure IT requirements are built in from the start and that Operations is ready to take ownership on Day 1.
Success in this role requires strong organizational leadership, disciplined service management, financial acumen, and the ability to turn technical and operational risk into clear, decision-ready recommendations for metro, regional and CO+I leadership. With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve to meet the business demands that make Microsoft a world-class cloud provider.
Do you want to empower billions across the world? Come and join us in CO+I and be at the forefront of the action!
Responsibilities
Organizational Leadership and People Management
Build, lead, coach and develop the Charlotte Metro IT Operations organization, including Datacenter Technician Managers, Datacenter Program Managers and Datacenter Technicians across all Class A and Class B facilities.
Deliver success through empowerment and accountability by modeling, coaching and caring. Live our culture, embody our values and practice our leadership principles.
Set the IT organization's strategy, priorities, operating rhythm, performance expectations and long-term capability roadmap in line with metro and CO+I priorities.
Lead IT workforce, capacity and succession planning across the metro. Allocate resources across campuses and sites based on business priority, infrastructure complexity, operational risk and future demand.
Attract, hire and retain great people. Know everyone's capabilities and aspirations, invest in the growth of others, and develop the next generation of leaders through intentional delegation and succession planning.
Make sure teams complete required training and certifications. Partner with Learning & Development to evolve the training portfolio as technology and site requirements change.
Recognize team successes and reward teamwork while keeping the culture focused on strategic goals.
2. IT Operations and Service Delivery
Own end-to-end service compliance, quality and client satisfaction for all IT services in the metro, against agreed SLAs, OLAs, KPIs and OKRs.
Oversee all IT operations activity, including server and rack deployment, network turn-up, structured cabling, break-fix and hardware repair, asset tracking, decommissions, and secure media handling and destruction.
Apply deep subject-matter expertise and escalate as needed to meet SLA/OLA commitments with minimal disruption to customers and the business. Review metrics with leaders so everyone understands targets and current performance.
Manage relationships with internal clients and service-line partners so expectations are clear and understood, and deliver solutions with a strong customer focus.
Understand future business demand in each facility so that IT staffing, tooling, spares and resources keep pace with growth.
Share common and recurring issues with regional and global teams, and promote best practices that prevent recurrence and make resolution more efficient.
3. IT Outfitting, Capacity Delivery and Operational Readiness
Own IT outfitting and infrastructure delivery for new builds, expansions, retrofits and live-site changes across all Class A and Class B facilities in the metro.
Make sure IT requirements are built into infrastructure designs and formal design reviews, including network, structured cabling, rack/enclosure layouts, power distribution to IT, maintainability, security and supportability.
Keep IT Operations engaged throughout construction and commissioning, including quality reviews, readiness assessments, commissioning participation and resolution of IT concerns before turnover.
Make sure documentation, procedures, spares, tooling, systems access, training and operational dependencies are in place before operational acceptance, so IT teams can safely and effectively take ownership on Day 1.
Support Go/No-Go and readiness decisions with clear, data-driven assessments of IT infrastructure and operational risk.
Ensure on-time, defect-free delivery of customer capacity within SLA commitments. Govern post-turnover stabilization, early-life performance and defect resolution.
Plan with business partners when carrying out their requirements so that datacenter availability, safety and security are maintained.
4. Incident Management, Reliability and Risk
Serve as the senior IT escalation point for the metro. Take part in, and lead where appropriate, every Sev 1 and Sev 2 incident bridge affecting Microsoft cloud services in Charlotte, including communication with customers and senior leadership.
Approve root-cause analyses and postmortem reports, and drive improvement plans and corrective and preventive actions to completion.
Prevent IT infrastructure and operational risk before it affects safety, security, availability, capacity delivery, cost or schedule, or creates long-term technical debt.
Use incident trends, hardware failure data, commissioning findings and field experience to find systemic risks. Partner with engineering, OEMs and vendors to resolve them.
Make sure IT work in live environments goes through rigorous change management, including risk assessment, Method of Procedure (MOP) and Emergency Operating Procedure (EOP) review, and maintenance-window planning, to protect customer availability.
Own the metro IT risk register and make sure risks, dependencies and ownership gaps are tracked, escalated and closed.
5. Financial and Vendor Management
Own the metro IT Operations budget, including detailed budgets, forecasts, and management of operating and capital spend. Make tradeoff decisions that follow sound fiscal practices.
Lead budget planning and demand-cost forecasting. Make sure business leaders understand how service-management issues affect cost, risk and staffing, and negotiate for the resources the organization needs.
Manage and oversee IT vendor and partner contracts and relationships, including IT service providers, contracted labor, OEMs and partner support teams. For leased facilities, coordinate with landlords and their operators on IT-related requirements.
Hold vendors accountable for performance, quality and commercial results, and recommend extra funding or resources for pilots, task forces or growth where needed.
6. Governance, Metrics and Executive Communication
Establish consistent IT Operations governance across the metro, with clear decision rights, escalation paths, response expectations and accountability.
Set and monitor meaningful KPIs. Examples include SLA attainment, on-time capacity delivery, readiness milestone completion, incident and repair turnaround, issue aging, turnover defect trends, asset accuracy, safety performance and cost efficiency.
Give the Metro Director and regional leadership concise reports on IT portfolio health, readiness, schedule, financial performance, risk and key decisions.
Translate complex technical and operational issues into clear, decision-ready information for senior leadership.
Represent IT Operations in metro, regional and CO+I leadership forums, design reviews and readiness governance.
7. Cross-Functional Partnership and One Microsoft
Serve as the single point of IT Operations integration for the metro across CE, IAM/Logistics, DCD, DCE, Commissioning, Physical Security, Environment Health & Safety, network and hardware engineering, and global and regional teams.
Partner with the Metro Director and peer functional leaders to align metro priorities, coordinate cross-campus planning, manage dependencies and resolve ownership gaps.
Find opportunities to collaborate across groups, make sure cross-team commitments are set, and achieve scale by enabling the work of others.
Support global and regional initiatives such as environmental health and safety programs, risk assessments, audits, compliance and certifications.
Act as a trusted advisor to a wide network of colleagues and bring diverse viewpoints together to solve organization-wide problems.
8. Safety, Security, Culture and Ownership
Build a culture of safety, security, quality, compliance and customer obsession in every part of IT operations.
Follow the runbooks provided by the Environment, Health & Safety division, and report any safety or security issue or concern immediately.
Take pride and personal accountability for end-to-end service quality, completeness and the resulting customer experience. Find unaddressed issues and resolve them, escalate them, or find the right owner.
Remove barriers to agility so teams can shift priorities quickly without losing productivity.
Learn, live and coach the One Microsoft culture and values. Lead through change by bringing clarity, generating energy and delivering success.

High School Qualification or equivalent AND 10+ years experience of mission-critical service management (e.g., providing IT services, manufacturing, warehouse, retail, military, or managing physical operations in an IT and/or critical environment infrastructure) OR equivalent experience
3+ years people management experience.

title: Director, Social & Creator Marketing - Minecraft
description:
Overview
At Mojang Studios, the creators of Minecraft, we are on a mission to build a better world through the power of play.
Why play? Well, play is at the heart of everything we do. It’s the blocky backbone of our games, the core of our development philosophy, and even the origin of our name. From the relentless experimentation of our endlessly inspiring community to the classrooms where Minecraft has become an essential teaching tool, play is the bedrock of our existence.
We enable millions to create and play together, connect people across the globe, and foster a community that is among the most active and passionate in the world. Our community is global and incredibly diverse. When we are developing anything within our franchise, we keep this in mind. We want everyone to not only feel included in Minecraft, but also to see themselves in what we make. Our goal is for the Mojang Studios team to be as diverse as our community.
Minecraft leads how Minecraft builds audiences, participates in culture, and deepens relationships with players, creators, and fans globally. The Director, Social & Creator Marketing is responsible for a connected global organization spanning organic social, including international and local market channels, influencer and community marketing, affiliate marketing and creator commerce, and editorial and direct-to-fan programming.
Exceptional cultural and creative judgment is essential. The leader must understand culture and community, recognize what is authentically Minecraft, and translate emerging audience and creator signals into distinctive ideas, stories, programming, and experiences that people want to watch, share, create with, and participate in.
The Director, Social & Creator Marketing works closely with Performance Marketing to connect these capabilities with paid media and player lifecycle marketing around shared audience, franchise, and business priorities. The leader builds the organization, talent, capabilities, partnerships, and ways of working needed to deliver impact on a global scale and compound that impact over time.

Responsibilities
Lead Minecraft’s global audience, influencer and community marketing strategy
Define how Minecraft builds audiences, participates in culture, and deepens relationships with players, creators, and fans. Set the vision, priorities and direction across organic social, influencer marketing, affiliate and creator commerce, community marketing, and direct-to-fan programming, connecting the work around shared audience, franchise, and business priorities.

Recognize what is authentically Minecraft and translate emerging cultural, audience, and creator signals into distinctive ideas, stories, programming, and experiences.
